newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti in for tough time at meetings.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti in for tough time at meetings.

text.p: Top executives at Italy's struggling hi-tech group Olivetti will come under tough questioning at analyst meetings on Thursday and Friday on the company's strategy for recovery.
Olivetti's new chief executive Roberto Colaninno will lead the company's team in the meetings with analysts and investors in Milan on Thursday at 1500 GMT and in London the following day at 0900 GMT.
Analysts say they will be looking for some clear pointers on group policy after the company has continually disappointed investors on when a recovery in its fortunes will come.

They will seek clarity over the position of its loss-making personal computer company, whether a float of its office equipment make Lexikon is still planned, and what is needed to stop margin erosion at its key systems and services company.

Olivetti, which has not made a profit since 1990, came under further pressure when its ex-director general in charge of finance and auditing Renzo Francesconi resigned in early September over his doubts on the first half results, while Olivetti's internal auditors critised the half year report.

Analysts said Olivetti would need to give some outline on how it would act to reduce its debts after it reported earlier this week that group net debt had increased in July and August to 2.39 trillion lire from 1.26 trillion at June 30.

They would also ask Olivetti if it planned any further board changes to introduce independent directors to represent shareholders interests, and if it had any plans for a capital restructuring at the group.
